# Prajnyavan (pj) — full reference

## What this is

Prajnyavan (binary name `pj`) is a Rust CLI that runs agentic coding sessions —
reading, writing, testing, and debugging code across multiple tool-call turns —
against a local Ollama model by default, with an optional escalation path to a
cloud provider (Anthropic or OpenAI) for harder problems.

The source is closed and lives in a private repository. This site, and the
pj-releases repo (https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases) it's part of, are
the public surface of the project: compiled binaries, install instructions, and
honest documentation of what currently works.

## What to actually expect from a local model

`pj chat` works best with a model that reliably emits structured tool calls (the
default, `qwen2.5-coder:7b`, does this reasonably well).

Bigger isn't always usable: `pj doctor` warns if an installed model is too large
for your RAM — a model needs headroom beyond its own size for the OS, context
cache, and everything else running. Check it before picking a model, not after
it gets OOM-killed mid-session.

Local models make real reasoning mistakes: wrong arithmetic in generated tests,
ignoring explicit instructions, inconsistent results on identical prompts.
`pj build` catches and retries build/test failures automatically, but it can't
catch every kind of mistake. For work where correctness matters more than
staying fully local, set `PJ_ESCALATE_PROVIDER` (`anthropic` or `openai`) to
hand off to a cloud model after a few stalled turns.

## Install

### Manual download (available now)

Grab the archive for your platform from the Releases page
(https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases/releases), verify it against the
accompanying `.sha256` file, extract, and put `pj` on your PATH:

```
curl -LO https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases/releases/download/v0.1.0/pj-0.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz
curl -LO https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases/releases/download/v0.1.0/pj-0.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz.sha256
shasum -a 256 -c pj-0.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz.sha256
tar -xzf pj-0.1.0-macos-arm64.tar.gz
sudo mv pj-0.1.0-macos-arm64/pj /usr/local/bin/pj
pj --help
```

Available today: macOS (arm64). macOS (x86_64) and Linux (x86_64) archives land
as they're built.

### Homebrew & npm (coming soon)

A Homebrew tap and an npm package are planned but not yet published to a public
tap/registry.

## Features — what actually works today

- CLI & daemon mode: `pj chat` / `pj build` for interactive use; `pj daemon`
  exposes workspace indexing and memory over JSON-RPC.
- Real sandboxing: OS-level confinement (macOS Seatbelt / Linux bubblewrap)
  restricts `execute_command` to the workspace and temp directories, with
  network access denied by default, plus execution auditing and redaction.
- Generate → verify → fix loop: `pj build` runs the project's real build/test
  command after scaffolding and asks the model to fix failures automatically,
  with a bounded retry count.
- `pj doctor`: checks installed Ollama models against available RAM and warns
  before you hit an OOM kill mid-session.
- OS keyring for API keys: `pj secret set/status/clear` stores cloud provider
  keys in the system keyring instead of a plaintext env var.

## Scaffolded, not yet wired up

- Plugins: manifests are parsed, validated, and permission-checked, and WASM
  modules load via `wasmtime` — but there's no ABI yet for actually invoking a
  plugin's code, so plugin tools report that explicitly rather than pretending
  to run.
- MCP (Model Context Protocol): types and an in-process JSON-RPC handler exist,
  but nothing connects `pj chat` to an external MCP server yet, and its own
  tool-execution endpoint isn't wired up either. `pj mcp add` / `pj mcp-server`
  say so explicitly rather than faking success.

## Architecture

A Rust workspace of purpose-built crates:

- pj-core — agent session, tool loop
- pj-cli — entry point, commands
- pj-providers — Ollama/Anthropic/OpenAI
- pj-protocol — shared value/message types
- pj-security — permissions, redaction
- pj-execution — sandboxed command execution
- pj-memory — short-term context
- pj-persistence — SQLite-backed storage
- pj-code-index — workspace code search
- pj-orchestration — multi-phase task pipeline
- pj-plugins — WASM plugin loading
- pj-mcp — Model Context Protocol scaffolding
- pj-batch — batch job handling
- pj-intelligence — higher-level reasoning helpers
- pj-templates — project scaffolding templates
- pj-monitor — runtime monitoring
- pj-macros — shared proc-macros

## Source & releases

The application source is closed. What's public:

- prajnyavan/pj-releases (https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases) — compiled
  binaries only, published via CI from the private source at tagged commits.
- Releases (https://github.com/prajnyavan/pj-releases/releases) — every
  published version, with `.sha256` checksums alongside each archive.
